question.problem:
Let $a=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$, $b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]$ and $c=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$ Find $\,4a-(3b-2c).$
$4a-(3b-2c)=\,\,$ {{field-1}}
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
To compute the result, we just need to perform the required operations with each component separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}4a-(3b-2c) & =4\,[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-(3\,[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]-2\,[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-20 \\ 12\end{aligned}]-([\begin{aligned}6 \\ -12\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 12\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-20 \\ 12\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -24\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-28 \\ 36\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
